It also covers topics such as entrepreneurship, innovation, and venture capital.

feeds.title: Gust Blog
feeds.description: Gust is the online collaboration space for early stage finance, from pitch to exit. As the world's largest fundraising platform and community. Gust enables skilled entrepreneurs to collaborate with the smartest investors and angel investor networks by virtually supporting all aspects of the investment relationship, from initial pitch to successful exit. Follow this blog to get thoughts on startups by investors who fund them & entrepreneurs who run them.

feeds.title: UK Business Angels Association
feeds.description: We strive to build and connect the investment ecosystem, creating a coherent and diverse landscape for financing high-potential entrepreneurs across the whole of the UK. Our members include angel groups, individual investors, early-stage VCs, equity investment platforms, family offices, universities, and accelerators.

feeds.title: Irrus Investments
feeds.description: Read the latest news articles and items of interest posted by Irrus Investment Syndicate. Irrus is devoted to helping forward-thinking innovators, creators, and entrepreneurs with the mentorship and funding that fuels success. Our member-led organization offers early-stage companies an opportunity to harness the insights and experience of more than 40 successful entrepreneurs, senior executives, technologists, and skilled professionals from a diverse set of industries.

feeds.title: Henley Business Angels
feeds.description: Find out more about our latest investment news and feature pieces, as well as information about our upcoming events. HBA, which operates from Henley Business School at the University of Reading, is a network of experienced business leaders, successful entrepreneurs, and investors. The network's aim is to facilitate opportunities for members to invest in and mentor (S) EIS-registered early-stage businesses launched by entrepreneurs who graduated from or are connected with the Henley Business School and the University of Reading.
